# External oversight of military AI: verified authorities and implementation
Research date: 13 November 2026. Public documents only. No contact, form submission, procurement, or login. This report is not evidence of ASIMOV-specific oversight.

## Principal answer
Independent checking is possible within government and by Congress's auditors, but access, independence, technical scope and public disclosure are separate questions. A research benchmark does not become an operational-weapons approval merely because it has government evaluators. Conversely, restricted public release does not establish that no independent official can inspect the results.

## 1. DOT&E: independent from acquisition, not outside the Pentagon
[10 USC139](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-120/t10/s139/) (text through PL119-120, 7 October2026): subsection(c) makes director/staff independent of acquisition officials and permits direct communication to SecDef without their concurrence. Sections(b)(8), (e)(1)-(4) provide approved test-plan access, prompt operational test results, observers, all DoD records the director considers necessary and modeling/simulation verification/validation data. Section(d) separates developmental test responsibilities. Section(h) requires annual reporting to Congress and, for classified/CUI reports, a concurrent unclassified version without dissemination controls; (i) requires compliance with congressional requests. These are substantive oversight powers, not guaranteed public access to underlying test datasets. They do not demonstrate that DOT&E inspected ASIMOV or any named system in that program.

[GAO-26-108859, 30June2026](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-26-108859), report pp1-2 and briefing enclosure: actual reorganization reduced civilian/action-officer staffing while oversight workload rose; staff reported expertise/capacity shortfalls. Contractor stoppage disrupted data access approximately two months; reduced secure workspace complicated classified oversight. GAO recorded concerns about undocumented system shortfalls and whether rapid acquisition could outpace testing. This is evidence of institutional strain, not a finding that a particular ASIMOV weapon escaped review. Report combines record review and interviews, not a census of dangerous weapons.

## 2. Congress: unusually concrete statutory reporting hooks
[PL118-159, FY2025 NDAA §1066, 138Stat2070-2071](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-118publ159/html/PLAW-118publ159.htm): defense committees must receive annual reports by 31December2025, terminating 31December2029. Required lists cover lethal autonomous systems approved under DoDD3000.09; waived senior review; undergoing review; and not approved. Initial reporting period is all relevant prior periods as determined by Secretary. Reports are unclassified with optional classified annex.

[PL119-60, FY2026 NDAA §1061, 139Stat1045](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/PLAW-119publ60/html/PLAW-119publ60.htm) adds legal reviews to the waived/under-review/not-approved lists. Its enacted [10USC130g](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-120/t10/s130g-1/) requires written notification within30days of any DoDD3000.09 waiver, including rationale, system/technology and anticipated duration; unclassified with optional classified annex. This is LAW, not the separate June2026 proposed responsible-AI legislation. No delivered reports/notifications were located in this research. That is an unverified delivery/publication status, not proof of noncompliance. Submission to committees is not a public-release guarantee. These specific records could connect safeguards to actual weapon systems more directly than research papers.

## 3. GAO: demonstrated outside-DoD audit, not a weapons certifier
[31USC716](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-120/t31/s716/) permits access needed for audit/evaluation/investigation, with request/escalation and litigation mechanisms. Section(d) limits litigation/subpoena enforcement for certain intelligence records, statutory exclusions or specified presidential/OMB certifications. Section(e) obliges equivalent confidentiality. Congressional audit access therefore does not imply publication of all evidence.

[GAO-27-107837, 14October2026](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-27-107837), report pp8-12, methodology pp13-14/AppendixIII: council meetings lapsed late2024–August2025; officials said just3/10 authorized Responsible AI Division posts were filled February2026. Most surveyed components had taken initial implementation/oversight steps. Both new recommendations (council charter, staffing needs) remain marked open on the official page; DoD concurred. The survey comprised ten selected use cases, one each in Army,Navy,AirForce,SpaceForce,Marines,DIA,NGA,DTRA,SOCOM,CyberCommand; selected from378 inventory entries. It is explicitly nongeneralizable. DARPA/ASIMOV was not one of those ten component cases. This establishes functioning scrutiny and documented gaps, not ASIMOV failure or department-wide absence of responsible AI.

## 4. Inspector General
[5USC406](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-120/t5/s406/) supplies timely records access and audit/investigative powers. [5USC408(b)](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-120/t5/s408/) contains an important qualification: SecDef may restrict audits/investigations/access concerning sensitive operational plans, intelligence and other national-security matters; exercising this power triggers statements to Congress within specified30day periods. The statute's amendment notes update committee names. The office is not an unrestricted external watchdog, but neither is it merely the developer marking its own homework.

Official indexed result confirms [29June2026 IG follow-up project announcement D2026-DEV0SI-0108.000](https://www.dodig.mil/Reports/Audits-and-Evaluations/Article/4532355/project-announcement-follow-up-evaluation-on-artificial-intelligence-recommenda/). Direct page returned403. Treat only as an announced follow-up, not completed results or ASIMOV audit.

## 5. Public access to DOT&E: consequential, verification bounded
Official search-index text of [DOT&E About](https://www.dote.osd.mil/About/About-DOT-E/) currently describes publicly releasable annual reporting and directs Common Access Card holders to an extranet for unclassified reports. [Norcross official press release](https://norcross.house.gov/press-releases?ID=E4B6DD53-7B47-4924-956C-ED9BF0BFB0BA) describes Warren/Norcross seeking restoration of annual reports by26August2026. Direct fetches of both pages and the publications page returned403 in this environment. This corroborates an access controversy through indexed primary sources; it is NOT a comprehensive current accessibility test, proof every PDF is inaccessible, or proof of legal violation. Search still indexes the FY2025 annual PDF. A denied fetch here must not be described as proof Pentagon withdrew it. Do not equate unclassified, publicly releasable, publicly posted, and open reproducible evidence.

## Suggested reporting questions (not executed)
- Were §1066 annual reports delivered for2025? Can committee/DoD release their unclassified portions and dates of transmission? What system/review categories are included/excluded?
- Have §130g waiver notices been issued; what scope/duration/rationale? No assumption a waiver exists.
- Was any ASIMOV candidate designated for operational oversight? Who had access to test configurations, failure cases and uncertainty estimates? Were acceptance tests independent from developer training?
- Which ASIMOV results reached legal reviewers, operational evaluators or acquisition authorities? A technical safeguard demonstration and a legal review answer different questions.

## Method and limitations
Searched official statutes, GAO, DOT&E, IG, congressional sites; preferred enacted text over bills/press summaries. Downloaded original official HTML/PDF where available; pdftotext extracts for reading; no modification of originals. GAO briefing attachment pages are image-only in standard text extraction; detailed numerical staffing claims beyond first-page narrative were not relied on. DoDD3000.09 official PDF fetch failed403, so no independent section-by-section assertion here. Parent may add an independently obtained copy. Search snippets support only flagged limited claims above. Manifest includes SHA256 and URL. No inference from public non-discovery to absence of confidential oversight.
